definition: Stable project identifier for the included study.
extraction_rule: Prefill from the accepted study mapping and do not alter during article extraction.
format_or_allowed_values: MSCR-R001 to MSCR-R031; unique; blank, NI, and N/A prohibited.
source_or_basis: Accepted project record mapping.

definition: Identifier for the included record in EPPI-Reviewer.
extraction_rule: Prefill from the accepted record mapping and retain as text.
format_or_allowed_values: Eight digits; unique; blank, NI, and N/A prohibited.
source_or_basis: Accepted EPPI-Reviewer mapping.

definition: First-author surname or group-author label used for the study citation label.
extraction_rule: Prefill from the accepted article byline; preserve spelling and diacritics.
format_or_allowed_values: Text; blank, NI, and N/A prohibited.
source_or_basis: Accepted bibliographic metadata.

definition: Publication year of the included version of record.
extraction_rule: Prefill from the article citation; do not substitute an indexing or online-first year for the included version-of-record year.
format_or_allowed_values: Four digits; blank, NI, and N/A prohibited.
source_or_basis: Accepted bibliographic metadata.

definition: Published title of the included article.
extraction_rule: Prefill from the accepted citation; preserve wording and punctuation, normalising whitespace only.
format_or_allowed_values: Text; blank, NI, and N/A prohibited.
source_or_basis: Accepted bibliographic metadata.

definition: Design of the complete eligible study, independent of any selected efficacy result.
extraction_rule: D-164 scope for every scientific field: describe the complete eligible investigation and its relevant comparison conditions. Where the report also contains a separable component using menthol as a pain-model reference, keep that component's participants, exposures, purposes, and all findings in linked article evidence, outside the core values. Establish this separation from source-defined experimental purpose and context, not concentration or observed response. Do not automatically exclude healthy volunteers, induced-pain analgesia experiments, ordinary relevant controls, or mechanism-only cohorts. Retain eligible clinical pain-effect investigations even when the original hypothesis was exacerbation; improvement, worsening, and no change are equally eligible under the remaining rules. Classify from the reported study design supported by its complete allocation structure, arms, and periods. Parallel groups use different participants in separate groups, which may be non-concurrent; preserve the reported allocation schedule in evidence; Cross-over assigns the same participants different conditions across periods; Pre-post is organised around a before-and-after intervention comparison; Single arm is an uncontrolled one-group intervention trial; Case report is a clinical account of individual patients. Do not relabel a nominal single-arm trial merely because it reports longitudinal or before-and-after outcomes. Conversely, having one uncontrolled group alone does not establish Single arm when the study is organised as a before-and-after evaluation. Use NI when the report cannot establish the design.
format_or_allowed_values: Parallel groups; Cross-over; Pre-post; Single arm; Case report; or NI. N/A prohibited.
source_or_basis: Parker and Berman terminology, adapted under FR-C05 and D-079. D-164 separable pain-model reference scope, applied across scientific fields.

definition: Each distinct concise source-near pain condition or deliberately induced stimulus represented in the eligible study.
extraction_rule: Review the whole study, retain every eligible condition or stimulus once in source order, and do not replace the source-near description with a broad context label.
format_or_allowed_values: Text entries separated by literal '; '; whole or scoped NI allowed; N/A prohibited.
source_or_basis: Article evidence, D-103, and D-104.

definition: Each distinct broad pain origin paired with its controlled clinical or experimental context.
extraction_rule: Review the whole study and retain every eligible origin-context pair once. Use Induced when the study deliberately creates the pain or threshold stimulus and Pre-existing when the pain exists or is expected independently of the menthol test exposure.
format_or_allowed_values: Induced or Pre-existing: context; contexts: Arthritis, Breastfeeding, Cancer treatment, Carpal tunnel, Chemical, Dysmenorrhea, Electrical, Exercise, Headache, Hemodialysis treatment, Low back, Migraine, Musculoskeletal, Myofascial pain, Neuropathic cold allodynia, Post-surgical, Postherpetic neuralgia, Pressure, Sprain, Thermal, Ischaemia; distinct pairs separated by literal '; '; whole-cell NI allowed, not a context category or an extra entry beside known pairs; a new context requires rule review; N/A prohibited.
source_or_basis: Project context categories under FR-C05, D-051, and D-104. D-142 adds Electrical for explicitly induced electrical pain.

definition: Each distinct pain-related measurement construct paired with its scale or response-method family.
extraction_rule: Retain every eligible construct-method pair used in the study, whether or not it supplies a complete effect estimate. Intensity measures how much pain is experienced; Threshold measures the stimulus level at which pain begins or reaches a defined point. Use a method family only when supported by the instrument or procedure. For stimulus-threshold tests, retain the reported participant response method, such as Verbal report or Button press, with the stimulus apparatus and units in evidence. Use Threshold: NI if that response method is unidentified. An algometer force reading alone does not make the normalised method Force measurement; retain the supported force-defined pain-tolerance endpoint under D-142. Pain drawing requires a participant-completed anatomical chart or body map that supplies the measure, not an examiner's drawing or a mark on a VAS line. Retain NI for an unidentified applicable method. Other constructs remain concise and source-near. Retain an explicitly labelled pain-related composite even when its inseparable pain/non-pain result is excluded from analgesic efficacy counts; do not infer unreported component content.
format_or_allowed_values: <construct>: <method>; store the method labels BPI (Brief Pain Inventory), Button press, Force measurement, LANSS (Leeds Assessment of Neuropathic Symptoms and Signs), LMS (labelled magnitude scale), McGill PQ (McGill Pain Questionnaire), NPSI (Neuropathic Pain Symptom Inventory), NRS (numeric rating scale), ODI (Oswestry Disability Index), OHIP-14 (Oral Health Impact Profile), Pain drawing, PCS (Pain Catastrophising Scale), RMDQ (Roland-Morris Disability Questionnaire), Ruler measurement, Storr's scale, VAS (visual analogue scale), Verbal report, WOMAC (Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Arthritis Index), or NI, without the parenthetical explanations. Distinct pairs separated by literal '; '; <construct>: NI or whole-cell NI allowed; a bare NI cannot accompany known pairs; a new method requires rule review; N/A prohibited.
source_or_basis: FR-C07, FR-027, D-057, and the all-eligible adaptation in D-104. D-136 clarifies the distinct measurement and efficacy-count scopes. D-139 includes PCS and LANSS in this descriptive vocabulary, without including their cognitive/screening scores in efficacy counts. D-142 adds Force measurement for explicitly pain-limited tolerance; D-143 adds ODI under the D-138 pain-impact rule. D-147 adds Ruler measurement for explicitly pain-free mouth opening and OHIP-14 for descriptive measurement, without making its mixed total an analgesic efficacy outcome. D-148 adds WOMAC for its explicitly identified pain subscale without changing efficacy scope. D-165 adds RMDQ for source-supported back-pain-related disability under D-138; descriptive recording does not bypass efficacy comparison safeguards.

definition: Design-appropriate number of unique participants in the complete eligible investigation.
extraction_rule: Count all eligible unique people randomised for a randomised parallel or cross-over study, allocated or enrolled at the start of a non-random controlled study, starting the eligible menthol intervention in a pre-post or single-arm study, or described in a case report. Count each person once across eligible arms and periods; in cluster studies count people, not clusters. Do not substitute analysed or completer counts. Use NI when the governing number is not reported. Apply the D-164 scope in study_design: retain relevant eligible controls, but do not add people described solely in a separable menthol pain-model reference component. A reference exposure on an eligible participant does not remove that person from the eligible denominator. Preserve overall and component-specific totals in evidence.
format_or_allowed_values: Non-negative whole number or NI; N/A prohibited.
source_or_basis: FR-C04 and D-080.

definition: Denominator basis represented by sample_size.
extraction_rule: Use randomised for a randomised parallel or cross-over study, allocated_or_enrolled for a non-random controlled study, started_eligible_menthol_intervention for a pre-post or single-arm study, or persons_described for a case report. Determine the basis even when sample_size is NI. Use the complete eligible investigation under D-164, not a design created by adding a separate pain-model reference component.
format_or_allowed_values: randomised; allocated_or_enrolled; started_eligible_menthol_intervention; or persons_described. Blank, NI, and N/A prohibited.
source_or_basis: FR-C04 and D-080.

definition: Sex category for the population represented by sample_size.
extraction_rule: Classify the governing study population as female only, male only, or containing more than one reported sex or gender category; use NI when it cannot be established.
format_or_allowed_values: Female; Male; Mixed; or NI. N/A prohibited.

definition: Country or countries in which study participants were enrolled or studied.
extraction_rule: Use, in order, an explicit conduct country or site, a named institution or site plus authoritative location lookup, a registry or protocol, and author affiliation only as a last resort. Record conduct location, not author nationality or publication origin. Use English short country names and apply the preferred-name overrides below; do not retain an abbreviation or alternative spelling when a preferred name is established. Preserve the source wording and any location inference in evidence. Identify countries through the unchanged frozen WHO mapping and retain each country once, regardless of source-name variants. If an additional conduct country remains unresolved alongside a known country, add one bare NI entry.
format_or_allowed_values: English short country names separated by literal '; '; bare NI may stand alone or appear as a separate entry; scoped NI and N/A prohibited. Preferred English short-name overrides (ISO3): GBR=United Kingdom | IRN=Iran | TUR=Turkey | USA=United States.
source_or_basis: FR-014, accepted country hierarchy, D-109, and D-166 English short-name normalisation; frozen WHO identities and regions remain unchanged.

definition: WHO region or regions mechanically derived from country.
extraction_rule: Map every known country through the frozen WHO mapping, preserve country order, deduplicate, and propagate each bare NI entry; do not extract or judge the region independently.
format_or_allowed_values: Store codes only: AFR (African Region), AMR (Region of the Americas), SEAR (South-East Asia Region), EUR (European Region), EMR (Eastern Mediterranean Region), WPR (Western Pacific Region). Distinct codes separated by literal '; '; bare NI stands alone or mirrors a corresponding unresolved country entry; N/A prohibited.
source_or_basis: Official frozen WHO mapping, FR-013, and D-109.

definition: Physical form in which each eligible topical menthol- or peppermint-containing intervention was applied.
extraction_rule: Where a separate carrier exists, use the applicable Barnes form or vehicle term. Where none exists, retain a clear source-near non-vehicle physical form. Record each form once per study, never relabel ground plant material as an extract, and route a genuinely new form for rule review. Retain Peppermint oil for explicitly neat oil; classify its dilution in a separate oil carrier as Solution.
format_or_allowed_values: Ointment; Cream; Gel; Lotion; Solution; Foam; Spray; Ground peppermint; Ground menthol; Peppermint oil; distinct entries separated by literal '; '; whole or scoped NI allowed; N/A prohibited.
source_or_basis: Barnes vehicle terminology, FR-019, project non-vehicle extension, D-114, and the source-grounded D-137/D-140 extensions.

definition: Every distinct reported or reproducibly convertible menthol percentage for eligible topical preparations, linked to the reported purpose of menthol at that concentration.
extraction_rule: Retain direct points, ranges, and reproducible conversions with basis and qualifications. Preserve peppermint/product percentages without treating them as menthol percentages; never infer typical menthol content or invent endpoints. For each numeric or product-percentage entry append one aggregate purpose tag. Therapeutic means menthol is intended or investigated as a therapeutic component, including in a therapeutic comparator. Masking/control means menthol is included for masking or in an author-designated nominal placebo/control preparation without a stated therapeutic role for that menthol; it does not include every comparator arm. Follow the reported role of menthol, not the overall arm label when other ingredients are therapeutic. Neither label establishes biological activity or inactivity. Do not assign purpose from dose size or legacy composition-based comparator labels. Both requires source evidence that the same study, percentage, basis, and qualification serves both purposes, within or across preparations. Collapse repeated identical concentration entries and combine their evidenced purposes before tagging; purpose alone must not multiply plotted points. Use Both when both purposes are evidenced, even if another represented preparation remains unclear. Otherwise use purpose NI if any represented purpose remains unresolved after checking, retaining known purpose and uncertainty in evidence. Pending review is an explicitly temporary migration marker for existing values whose purpose has not yet been checked, never a scientific NI or a permitted completed article return. Preserve the preparation-to-value-to-purpose link and exact source locators in field_evidence. Bare or preparation-scoped NI for concentration remains untagged. Aggregate purpose tags do not determine efficacy eligibility; D-161 requires preparation-specific source evidence. Both or purpose NI may combine distinct preparations, and unavailable concentration does not establish unknown purpose. Retain masking/control preparations under this descriptive scope even when their standalone efficacy findings are excluded. Apply D-164 before collecting and aggregating core concentrations: preserve a separable menthol pain-model reference preparation in evidence, without forcing it into Therapeutic, Masking/control, Both, or purpose NI. Within a retained eligible clinical investigation, Therapeutic includes investigation of menthol's effects on existing pain or pain sensitivity even when exacerbation was hypothesised; preserve that hypothesis rather than claiming intended pain relief. A shared concentration is retained once for its eligible use; excluded reference use does not alter its aggregate purpose tag.
format_or_allowed_values: Separate entries with literal ; . Numeric examples: 4% menthol (w/w) [Purpose: Therapeutic]; approximately 2% menthol (basis not reported) [Purpose: NI]; 2% menthol (w/w, converted from 2 g menthol in 100 g preparation) [Purpose: Therapeutic]; 1-5% menthol (basis not reported) [Purpose: Both]; 10% peppermint oil (menthol concentration not established) [Purpose: Masking/control]. Preserve a reported peppermint/product basis before the menthol-concentration qualification. Bases: w/w, w/v, v/v, v/w, or basis not reported. Purpose labels: Therapeutic, Masking/control, Both, NI. Transitional existing-form label only: Pending review. One aggregate tag per numeric/range/product entry. NI or NI (<preparation>) denotes unavailable concentration and takes no purpose tag. N/A prohibited.
source_or_basis: D-117 concentration retention, conversion, and point unit; D-157 purpose linkage and interim migration. Article methods, formulation descriptions, and formal supplements; reported intent does not prove activity or inactivity. D-158 separately governs the reported role of the complete comparator regimen. D-161 separately applies a preparation-specific therapeutic-purpose boundary to efficacy findings. D-164 defines eligible investigation versus separate pain-model reference scope.

definition: Each distinct anatomical site to which an eligible topical menthol or peppermint intervention was applied.
extraction_rule: Prefer direct application wording. Use contextual inference only where the application site is unambiguous; do not substitute the pain site merely because it is reported. Retain each site once per study.
format_or_allowed_values: Concise source-near text entries separated by literal '; '; whole or scoped NI allowed; N/A prohibited.
source_or_basis: FR-021, D-029, and the all-eligible rule in D-103.

definition: Each substantive outcome-relevant exposure delivered alongside menthol and common to the compared regimens within at least one eligible comparison.
extraction_rule: Remove the focal menthol and comparator components before deciding whether an exposure is common. Exclude inert masking or placebo components and additions confined to one arm. Record each named co-intervention once; use N/A only when evidence establishes that none applies anywhere, and NI when one may apply but usable information is insufficient. Where the report explicitly raises a possible outcome contribution from a reported trace masking component, retain it when shared with its effect uncertain; masking purpose alone does not establish inertness.
format_or_allowed_values: Concise named entries separated by literal '; '; NI may stand alone or appear as a separate bare or scoped entry alongside named entries; whole-cell N/A must stand alone.
source_or_basis: Cochrane comparator principles, D-047, and D-116. D-141 clarifies reported trace masking components with expressly uncertain outcome relevance.

definition: Every distinct eligible comparator regimen, with its source-near description, reported intended role, and controlled type kept together.
extraction_rule: Create one profile per genuinely distinct regimen. Collapse repetition across outcomes, times, models, or analyses, but retain distinct arms, formulations, doses, routes, timings, and scientifically distinct baseline occasions. Classify the complete comparator regimen relative to topical menthol after separating a genuinely shared substantive co-intervention, preserving that shared context in the description or evidence. Therapeutic means a preparation or modality intended or investigated as a therapeutic alternative, not proven effective. Control means a nominal placebo/masking or other listed reference condition, not proven biologically inactive. Use reported intended role and methods, not ingredient presence, dose magnitude, or an assumed efficacy threshold. Non-zero menthol in a nominal placebo does not force Therapeutic or type Menthol. Type Menthol requires therapeutic intent for menthol; preserve masking menthol and all reported ingredients in the description regardless of the controlled types. A comparator containing another intentionally therapeutic component remains Therapeutic even when its menthol is for masking: retain the therapeutic component type without automatically adding Menthol. The whole regimen role can differ from the menthol-purpose tag in menthol_concentration. Usual care denotes the reference condition, not a claim that its treatments are inactive; distinguish shared background care from a deliberately contrasted therapeutic alternative. Preserve multi-component regimens as one profile, with all applicable therapeutic types. These descriptive roles do not determine efficacy-comparison eligibility or remove treatment-component safeguards. Check source coverage and omissions for all eligible regimens, and preserve source locators, ingredients, intended roles, and qualifications in evidence. Existing Active/Inactive entries are legacy classifications requiring source review, not automatic recoding. An unresolved broad role requires focused review; preserve source limitations or genuine pending scientific decisions explicitly rather than guessing. Under D-161, assess therapeutic purpose for menthol or peppermint in the actual comparison, not from the whole-regimen role alone. Preserve descriptive comparator coverage even when a corresponding efficacy finding is excluded. Apply the D-164 eligible-investigation scope. A separate menthol pain-model reference remains outside core comparator profiles; preserve it as evidence context rather than a therapeutic or nominal-placebo regimen. Preserve all of its reported exposures and findings in evidence. Ordinary relevant control regimens remain eligible under their own rules.
format_or_allowed_values: <description> [Therapeutic: <type>] or <description> [Control: <type>]; join types within one regimen with ' + ' and profiles with literal '; '. Control types: Nominal placebo/masking, No treatment, Pre-intervention baseline, Usual care. Therapeutic types: Breast milk, Heat, Ice, Lanolin, Rosemary, Menthol, Diclofenac, Dexpanthenol, Paracetamol, Capsaicin, Eucalyptus. Retain partial information, for example NI [Control: Nominal placebo/masking] or <description> [Therapeutic: NI]. Type NI must stand alone within its profile. Whole-cell NI or a separate NI (<unresolved regimen>) entry is allowed; bare NI cannot be mixed with known profiles. Whole-cell N/A means no eligible comparator and must stand alone. Repeated profiles or types are prohibited, including the same profile with reordered types. Legacy Active/Inactive tags are not current completed-return syntax.
source_or_basis: D-158 reported comparator role supersedes the D-058/D-118 non-zero-menthol composition convention in the active results-first workspace. D-118 retained regimen scope, deduplication, linked profile, missingness, and unpaired study memberships; D-157 separately records menthol purpose. D-159 implements the role grammar and preparation stop boundary. D-161 separately governs the efficacy therapeutic-purpose boundary. D-163 adds the source-established therapeutic comparator type Eucalyptus, retaining masking peppermint and combination regimens under D-158. D-164 separable pain-model reference scope.

definition: Confirmed minimum number of distinct explicitly reported eligible comparisons and descriptive case-report pain findings.
extraction_rule: Use the included primary article and formal supplements. Identify a comparison only when the authors communicate a study comparative finding identifying the compared conditions and eligible pain outcome through wording, labels, annotations, or statistical results. Source context can clarify identity; study design or separate arm/condition values alone cannot create a comparison. Neither significance nor a numerical estimate is required. Scoped qualitative or p-value-only findings may qualify; a detached p value does not identify or enumerate comparisons. Preserve broad or unspecified scope without inventing detail or requiring exact timing. Do not expand omnibus tests into unreported pairwise comparisons, broad statements into every occasion, or separate before/after findings into an unreported between-arm change. Include eligible comparisons with a control/reference condition, intended therapeutic alternative, or pre-intervention condition; an intended therapeutic alternative may replace menthol. Comparator role describes reported intent and does not by itself establish comparison eligibility. Under D-161, a counted finding must address menthol or peppermint intended or investigated as a therapeutic component in at least one compared condition. Exclude findings confined to preparations whose menthol or peppermint serves solely a masking/control purpose, including standalone before/after responses; another therapeutic ingredient does not confer therapeutic purpose on menthol. Therapeutic menthol versus a masking control may qualify under the remaining rules. Establish purpose for the actual preparation and comparison from source evidence, not dose magnitude, the whole-regimen role, or aggregate concentration-purpose tags. Preserve masking preparations descriptively; this boundary establishes neither biological inactivity nor study ineligibility. Retain unresolved preparation-specific purpose in evidence under the existing confirmed-count rules. Exclude planned-only outcomes, standalone pre-exposure differences, analyses principally about another treatment, and comparisons where an additional outcome-relevant component changes beyond the intended contrast unless shared. Exclude general aggregate or heterogeneity analyses that do not estimate the topical-menthol comparison, retaining the Section 05 scope. An omnibus label alone neither includes nor excludes a finding: check its actual treatment contrast and scope before counting it or assessing availability. A general equality test jointly comparing menthol with two non-menthol treatment groups does not itself identify a menthol-specific contrast; inclusion of a menthol arm alone does not make that aggregate eligible. Assess any separately reported focal menthol contrast on its own. This does not exclude an explicit within-menthol time-profile finding or a direct menthol-versus-comparator effect across occasions. Exclude inseparable pain/non-pain composites; retain separately reported eligible pain results without inventing components. Include pain-only composites, direct pain-attributed interference, total BPI, and their reported response rates. Explicitly pain-free mouth opening is eligible; generic mouth opening is not. Exclude generic function, mood, cognition, and diagnostic screening. Group repeated presentations and alternative analyses of the same comparison. Identify scope by treatment contrast/regimen, shared co-intervention, target population, pain measure/outcome definition, task/site, and assessment occasion or scope. Retain genuinely distinct reported comparators, occasions, instruments, and response thresholds. Unit conversions add no result. Adjusted/unadjusted or intention-to-treat/per-protocol labels alone do not establish sameness; equal or different estimates alone do not resolve grouping. Group a between-arm final-score comparison with its baseline-to-that-visit change comparison only when they address the same treatment effect, pain measure, target population, and follow-up occasion; do not generalise across designs or intervals. A within-menthol change differs from a between-treatment comparison. A defined cumulative/time-profile result differs from a recap of counted visits. Retain the full scope of an explicitly reported condition effect spanning pre- and post-treatment; do not relabel it as post-treatment-only. In descriptive case reports, count explicit pain responses or assessments following eligible topical menthol or peppermint used as a therapeutic component, even without a comparator or numerical change. Preserve the other eligibility/grouping rules, count improvement/no change/worsening alike, and assign no automatic result per patient or report. Apply this exception to actual descriptive design, not sample size alone. Record the confirmed distinct inventory even when additional findings may exist; keep possible additions, duplication uncertainty, source gaps, and checking attempts in evidence. Use 0 only after adequate checking finds no qualifying finding, and NI only when neither a positive confirmed count nor a supported zero is established. Do not conceal a pending scientific decision as NI. Missing estimates or precision do not remove a qualifying finding; inclusion does not establish causality. Apply D-164 before inventory identification: exclude standalone findings from a separable menthol pain-model reference component, preserving favourable, null, and adverse-direction findings alike in evidence. Retain otherwise eligible clinical investigations of menthol's effects on existing pain or pain sensitivity even when the stated hypothesis was exacerbation. Neither high concentration nor an unexpected beneficial response changes source-defined purpose. The descriptive-case exception does not override this scope.
format_or_allowed_values: Non-negative whole number or NI; blank and N/A prohibited. A numeric value equals the confirmed grouped inventory size, including 0. Retain confirmed positives despite uncertainty about additions. No automatic NI propagation to other fields; apply their own rules.
source_or_basis: D-150 explicit reporting; D-151 grouping; D-152 iterative method; D-153 confirmed minimum/zero/NI; D-155 descriptive cases. Retained Section 05 outcome/component scope, including D-136, D-138, and D-147. D-161 therapeutic-purpose boundary, with descriptive masking-control retention. D-164 narrow pain-model reference boundary.

definition: Confirmed number of counted comparisons with at least one usable reported or directly calculable numerical effect estimate.
extraction_rule: Assess the same confirmed grouped inventory as efficacy_result_count. Any permitted analysis representation or supported direct calculation within a comparison may establish availability; count that comparison once. Compatible reported arm/condition quantities can quantify an already identified comparison but cannot create one. Preserve the supporting representation, effect, inputs, population, occasion, units, and formula. Do not substitute an unrelated effect, model, impute, digitise graphs, or invent inputs, denominators, or correlations. A p value, test statistic, direction, or qualitative statement alone is insufficient. Clearly labelled graphical contrast estimates count as reported estimates without digitisation or a requirement for printed numerical labels (D-141). Recognising a reported estimate is distinct from extracting its magnitude. A labelled graphical contrast can also establish comparison reporting; separate arm plots alone cannot create a comparison or supply digitised quantities. A numerical effect of zero is available. Missing precision does not remove an estimate. Retain the number with confirmed availability despite unresolved availability elsewhere in the counted inventory. Use 0 after adequate checking finds none available, and NI only when neither positive availability nor a supported zero is established. Record uncertainty in linked evidence rather than treating it as absence. Use N/A for descriptive case reports because this comparative reporting assessment does not apply, even when their first count is 0 or NI; numerical observations or calculable changes may still be retained in evidence.
format_or_allowed_values: Non-negative whole number, NI, or descriptive-case-report N/A. Numeric count equals confirmed estimate-available inventory entries and cannot exceed a numeric efficacy_result_count. Case reports require N/A in both availability fields, independently of the first count. Non-case result count 0 requires both availability counts 0; estimate count 0 requires precision count 0. NI in this field does not automatically require precision NI. Blank prohibited.
source_or_basis: D-150 calculation boundary; D-151 grouped comparisons; D-153/D-154 confirmed availability and independent missingness; D-155 case-report scope. Supported-calculation safeguards retained from Section 05 and D-145.

definition: Confirmed number of counted comparisons with a usable estimate and its matching, design-appropriate precision.
extraction_rule: Use the same confirmed grouped inventory. Count a comparison once when any permitted analysis representation supplies both its usable estimate and matching confidence interval, standard error, or variance, reported or directly calculable from compatible supported information. The estimate and precision must belong to the same analysis, effect, population, occasion, and design. Grouped adjusted/unadjusted or final/change analyses must not exchange estimates and intervals. No modelling, imputation, graph digitisation, or unreported assumptions. Separate arm/time-point SDs count only when sufficient for the design; they alone do not supply paired-change or crossover precision. A p value alone is insufficient; never transfer omnibus tests to individual contrasts. Do not count an interval whose documented method fails to establish usable design-appropriate precision; retain the limitation without deleting the comparison or available estimate. This is an information-availability assessment, not general risk-of-bias assessment or selection of a preferred estimate for synthesis. Retain confirmed availability despite uncertainty about additional availability; use 0 after adequate negative checking, and NI only when neither a positive count nor a supported zero is established. Every precision-qualified entry must also have an available estimate. Use N/A for descriptive case reports independently of their first count. Later coverage uses the counted comparison inventory, not just comparisons with estimates, and is undefined when that inventory is 0. Percentages do not establish complete ascertainment or necessarily provide minimum whole-study percentages.
format_or_allowed_values: Non-negative whole number, NI, or descriptive-case-report N/A. Numeric count equals confirmed precision-available inventory entries. Where numeric, precision <= estimates <= results; a positive precision count entails positive confirmed estimate and result counts. If result count or estimate count is 0 in a non-case study, precision is 0. No automatic NI cascade. N/A must occur in both availability fields together, only for descriptive case reports. Blank prohibited.
source_or_basis: D-151 analysis compatibility; D-153 zero-denominator safeguard; D-154 matching precision and confirmed counts; D-155 case-report scope. Design-appropriate calculation safeguards retained from Section 05 and D-145.

definition: Public study-registration status and timing relative to first participant enrolment.
extraction_rule: Match the registry record using identifiers, title, intervention, investigators, sites, dates, and sample characteristics. Use first submission where available. Prospective means before the supported first-enrolment period; retrospective means after enrolment began or explicitly registered while recruiting. Preserve partial-date uncertainty; do not invent exact dates. After the bounded search, use the qualified no-match label rather than concluding that the study was never registered. Use NI when a match exists but timing is unresolved, or the search cannot establish a classification.
format_or_allowed_values: Prospective; Retrospective; No sufficiently matched public registry record located; NI. One value. Blank and N/A prohibited.
source_or_basis: FR-C02 and accepted D-081 record-level mapping.

definition: Study-level description of adverse-event reporting across all eligible topical-menthol groups and exposure periods, including combination treatments.
extraction_rule: Check adverse-event, tolerability, and relevant withdrawal information. Use Events reported for any documented adverse event during eligible menthol exposure, regardless of causal attribution; this overrides negative statements. Use Explicitly no events reported only for a clear overall zero covering the relevant menthol groups and reported observation period without contradictory events. Use Limited or unclear information for tolerability-only, event-specific or treatment-related-only negatives, incomplete coverage, conflicts, uncertain exposure timing, or comparator-only reporting. Use NI only when no relevant information is identified. Ordinary planned pain outcomes are not automatically adverse events.
format_or_allowed_values: Events reported; Explicitly no events reported; Limited or unclear information; NI. Exactly one value. Blank and N/A prohibited in completed data, including case reports.
source_or_basis: Cochrane Handbook Chapter 19; project reporting categories applying FR-C11/FR-032.

definition: Concise account of the reported adverse-event information and its treatment, population, and observation scope.
extraction_rule: Summarise relevant events, negative or qualified statements, and conflicts. Clearly label different menthol regimens, combination treatments, periods, and comparator-only information. Retain reported event types, numbers and their units/denominators, timing, withdrawals or treatment changes, and investigator attribution where available. Do not invent counts, rates, denominators, causality, or broader negative findings. Do not substitute the overall sample size for an unstated safety denominator.
format_or_allowed_values: Readable text, usually a few sentences, or NI. Use NI if and only if adverse_event_reporting is NI; every other status requires substantive details. Blank and N/A prohibited in completed data.
source_or_basis: FR-C11/FR-033; source adverse-event, tolerability, and withdrawal reporting.
